title: openbao-config-mto values
description: Deliberately minimal. This chart is normally rendered by template-operator-v2 from the bootstrap chart's valuesTemplate, so any constraint here has to accept everything t-op-v2 can send -- including serviceAccounts/deployments arriving as JSON null when a tenant has no workloads yet. Only the switches consumed as string comparisons are constrained, because a near-miss there (yes / on / True / 1) silently disables a feature. serviceAccounts, deployments, tierCaps, transit.tierCaps and sso.tiers are left entirely unconstrained on purpose. pki.roles is the exception: it is constrained field-by-field, for the reason given on that key. The boolean forms mirror the bootstrap chart's _helpers.tpl: a boolean, or the quoted strings "true"/"false".

boolish.description: true or false, as a YAML boolean or as the quoted string "true"/"false". yes, on, off, 1, 0, True and TRUE are rejected, because they would be read as "not enabled" without warning.

comment-on-component: `component` is deliberately NOT constrained here. templates/_helpers.tpl already fails on an unknown component with a message naming the valid set, and a schema enum would pre-empt it with a vaguer error while duplicating the valid list in a second place. Schema covers only the switches that had no guard at all.

eso.description: A string, not a boolean: "enabled" or "disabled".

roles.description: PKI role catalog. Constrained field-by-field because every field is a pass-through to OpenBaoPKISecretEngineRole that the chart OMITS when absent, so a misspelling (allowedDomainTemplate, maxTTL, allowSubDomains) is not a no-op: it silently leaves bao's default in place, which for allow_ip_sans and require_cn is the permissive one. additionalProperties is false for exactly that reason — an unknown key here is always a typo or a field the chart does not plumb, and both need to fail rather than render.

nameTemplate.description: Bao role name; {tenant} is substituted. Must render unique across entries, and must render a valid RFC 1123 subdomain — it is also the OpenBaoPKISecretEngineRole name (as pki-<name>) and the cert-manager Issuer name, both of which the apiserver rejects otherwise.

allowedDomainsTemplate.description: Allowed cert names; {tenant} and {namespace} are substituted, once per tenant workload namespace. The union across namespaces is also the tenant CA's X.509 name constraints, which are frozen when the CA is created.

allowIpSans.description: Nothing else in the chart bounds an IP SAN — allowedDomains and the CA's permittedDnsDomains are both DNS-name constraints. bao's default is true; leave this false unless a workload presents certs by IP.

allowAnyName.description: true discards allowedDomains: the role issues for any name, bounded only by the CA's name constraints.

noStore.description: true stops bao storing issued certs. Bounds storage growth, but the viewer and audit-read SSO tiers list pki/certs and read pki/cert/<serial>, which then return nothing.

ttl.description: Bao duration string, e.g. "168h". Mirrors the OpenBaoPKISecretEngineRole CRD pattern exactly: a unit suffix is required. bao's own parser would take a bare integer as seconds, but the CR passes through admission first, so a bare integer renders clean and is rejected at apply — failing the tenant's whole TemplateInstance.

maxTtl.description: Bao duration string. Note the spelling: maxTtl, not maxTTL. Same CRD-mirroring pattern as ttl.

keyBits.description: Key size. Bounds mirror the OpenBaoPKISecretEngineRole CRD (0-8192); a value outside them renders clean and is rejected at apply.

safety.description: Deletion-policy guardrails: non-destructive deletion by default. Cluster-global: t-op-v2 renders every tenant with the same values.

deletionProtection.description: true (default): mounts, auth mounts and bao namespaces are retained in OpenBao when their CR is deleted or renamed. false: CR deletion destroys the bao object and the data under it. Only an exact false disables protection.

grantDeletionProtection.description: false (default): deleting a policy/role/group/alias CR deletes the bao object, so offboarding revokes access. true: grants are retained through CR deletion and render churn, at the cost of leaked grants on offboarding. Only an exact true enables retention.

token.description: Workload token defaults stamped onto every OpenBaoKubernetesAuthRole. `type` is enumerated because bao's default/default-service/default-batch resolve against the auth mount's tune, making token semantics depend on state this chart does not own. numUses is deliberately absent: bao accepts it on a batch token and silently ignores it.

type.description: service persists the token (renewable, revocable, enumerable, 4 storage writes per login). batch is HMAC-derived and never stored (0 writes, but no renewal and no revocation). Pair batch with a short ttl.
